passage: “‘Hope’ is the thing with feathers” is an 1861 poem by Emily Dickinson. In the poem, the speaker suggests that hope sustains people without asking anything of them in return: _____
prompt: Which quotation from the text most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “‘Hope’ is the thing with feathers - / That perches in the soul -”
“I've heard it in the chillest land - / And on the strangest Sea - / Yet - never - in Extremity, / It asked a crumb - of me.”
“And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard - / And sore must be the storm -”
“And sings the tune without the words - / And never stops - at all -”
expl: Only the last stanza says hope never asked for anything (“a crumb”). The others describe hope's presence and persistence, not that it costs nothing.

passage: “The Road Not Taken” is a 1916 poem by Robert Frost. In the poem, the speaker imagines looking back on the decision long after making it: _____
prompt: Which quotation from the text most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “I shall be telling this with a sigh / Somewhere ages and ages hence:”
“And both that morning equally lay / In leaves no step had trodden black.”
“Two roads diverged in a yellow wood, / And sorry I could not travel both”
“Then took the other, as just as fair, / And having perhaps the better claim,”
expl: “Ages and ages hence” is the only line about the future. The others describe the choice itself.

passage: In Jane Austen's 1813 novel *Pride and Prejudice*, Elizabeth Bennet acknowledges that her dislike of Mr. Darcy is connected to the way he has wounded her own self-regard. In a conversation with her sister, Elizabeth says, _____
prompt: Which quotation from the text most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “I could easily forgive his pride, if he had not mortified mine.”
“She is tolerable; but not handsome enough to tempt me.”
“It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.”
“Pride relates more to our opinion of ourselves, vanity to what we would have others think of us.”
expl: “Mortified mine” = he hurt her pride. The other lines are spoken by the narrator, Darcy, and Mary, and aren't about Elizabeth's feelings.

passage: In Mary Shelley's 1818 novel *Frankenstein*, the creature claims that his cruelty is the result of his suffering rather than of his original nature. Speaking to Victor Frankenstein, the creature says, _____

“Life, although it may only be an accumulation of anguish, is dear to me, and I will defend it.”
“I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend.”
“Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.”
expl: Two parts of the claim: originally good, and suffering changed him. Only “benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend” has both.

passage: In Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel *Jane Eyre*, Jane firmly asserts her right to make her own choices. Speaking to Mr. Rochester, she declares, _____

“I am no bird; and no net ensnares me: I am a free human being with an independent will.”
“There was no possibility of taking a walk that day.”
“I would always rather be happy than dignified.”
expl: “Free… independent will” is a direct assertion of autonomy, said to Rochester.

passage: In his 1845 *Narrative*, Frederick Douglass suggests that learning to read deepened his awareness of his enslavement without giving him a way to escape it. Douglass writes, _____

“You have seen how a man was made a slave; you shall see how a slave was made a man.”

Acacia trees with ants grew taller in years with heavy rainfall.

expl: If dolphins don't react specially to their own whistle, the “name” idea fails. The first two choices support it.

Animal bones at the site come almost entirely from species that pass through the area only during autumn migrations.
expl: Bones from one season only point to seasonal use. Durable houses would point to permanent settlement.

passage: Psychologists hypothesize that people remember material better when they explain it to someone else than when they study it alone.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the hypothesis?
choices: Participants who taught a lesson spent twice as much time preparing as those who studied alone.
Participants who studied alone said they felt more confident about the material.
Participants who taught a lesson to a partner recalled more of the material a week later than participants who studied it alone for the same amount of time.
Participants who taught a lesson reported enjoying the task more than those who studied alone.
expl: Better recall with equal time isolates teaching. Twice the prep time would be a confound, and enjoyment and confidence aren't memory.

expl: No pressure signs plus volcanic minerals point to a different origin. The other choices support an impact.

Chinese has many regional varieties with different pronunciations.
